bridges.label: Bridgy Fed
bridges.mode_note: Bridgy Fed mirrors one existing account into the other networks under a new bridged handle. It does not copy posts between two accounts you already have, so a native Mastodon account and a bridged Bluesky account are two separate presences in the fediverse.

enable.atmosphere: Log in at fed.brid.gy and click Enable, or follow @ap.brid.gy on Bluesky. The account then appears in the fediverse as @[handle]@bsky.brid.gy.
enable.fediverse: Log in at fed.brid.gy and click Enable, or follow @bsky.brid.gy@bsky.brid.gy from the fediverse account and accept its follow back.
enable.web: Enter the site at fed.brid.gy. Fediverse users then find it as @[domain]@web.brid.gy (or @[domain]@[domain] / @[domain]@fed.brid.gy).

bridges.disable: Block the Bridgy Fed bot for the network you want to leave: @bsky.brid.gy@bsky.brid.gy on the fediverse, @ap.brid.gy on Bluesky.

sources.quote: Bridgy Fed is opt in.
Bridgy Fed doesn't cross-post (ie copy posts) between separate accounts. Instead, it federates, or mirrors, your existing accounts into other networks.
Can I use this to bridge two existing accounts that I already have? Sorry, no, Bridgy Fed doesn't support this.
Alternatively, you can bridge your account by following @ap.brid.gy on the Atmosphere.
Bridgy Fed currently supports the web, fediverse, and the Atmosphere (Bluesky). We're considering adding more networks, including Farcaster and Nostr.

identity_checks.label: fediverse:creator author tag on your article pages
identity_checks.action: Add <meta name="fediverse:creator" content="@you@your.server"> to the <head> of pages you publish, so Mastodon credits your fediverse account when the link is shared. Mastodon shows the exact code under Preferences > Public profile > Verification > Author attribution.

sources.quote: The handle can be any fediverse account, not just Mastodon. That includes Flipboard, Threads, WordPress (with the ActivityPub plugin installed), PeerTube, Pixelfed, and many others.
This is possible by including a fediverse:creator tag in the HTML code of the websites where your work is published.

identity_checks.label: Verified link (rel="me") between your site and your Mastodon profile
identity_checks.action: Put your site's HTTPS URL in the Mastodon profile metadata and link back from the site to the profile with rel="me"; Mastodon then shows a verification checkmark next to that link.

sources.quote: If you put an HTTPS link in your profile metadata, Mastodon checks if that link resolves to a web page that links back to your Mastodon profile with a special rel=me attribute.

identity_checks.label: Your own domain as your Bluesky handle
identity_checks.action: In Bluesky: Settings > Account > Handle > I have my own domain, then add the _atproto TXT record it shows (did=did:plc:...) at your DNS host and click Verify DNS Record.

sources.quote: On Bluesky, you can set your website as your username. This is one form of verification on Bluesky.
Set the domain: _atproto Set the type: TXT

canonical_home_policy.rationale: Publish the full piece first at an address you control (your site, newsletter or ActivityPub blog), then share it on the networks. An owned address keeps working if a network changes its rules or algorithm, and with ActivityPub (Ghost 6, the WordPress plugin) or Bridgy Fed it can also be followed from the fediverse and Bluesky. This is a planning heuristic, not a measured reach result.
